primitives.name: Run Scheme Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Run Scheme Classification** (new for 2026 season) - Verbatim: "Our new run scheme classification model uses a transformer architecture to interpret the spatial and temporal relationships among players throughout a play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L': 'Label representing play design (16 discrete classes)', 'S': 'Spatial-temporal player configuration vector'}
primitives.assumptions: Transformer architecture assumes sequential dependency in player motion; 16-class labeling implies categorical output space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when player trajectories lack sufficient distinctiveness for classification.

layer2.mapping: Run scheme labels map to GSE state-action transition matrices via player position and velocity vectors.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of 16-label classification on per-play basis.

primitives.name: Route Classification 2.0
primitives.verbatim_quote: Route Classification 2.0** (2026) - Verbatim: "We debuted our original Route Recognition model in 2020.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R': 'Route type (shallow, deep, fade, go, screen, etc.)', 'P': 'Player trajectory path vector'}
primitives.assumptions: Route distinction relies on receiver motion patterns; screen detection requires blocker movement data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inaccurate classification when receiver paths overlap or are ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: Route types are embedded into GSE's kernel of receiver positioning and timing features.
layer2.telemetry: Precision of route type assignment per receiver per play.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Completion Probability** (debuted 2018) + CPOE - Verbatim (nfl.com, Sep 21, 2018): "Completion Probability is measured using more than 10 different in-play factors collected by Next Gen Stats player-tracking devices.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_c': 'Probability of completion (0–1)', 'F_i': 'Factor i (e.g., air distance, separation)'}
primitives.assumptions: XGBoost model trained on 10+ in-play metrics; assumes linear and non-linear combinations of features.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Model fails when unseen factor combinations exceed training domain.

layer2.mapping: Completion probability maps to GSI’s Bayesian posterior over pass outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Brier score or log-loss of predicted vs actual completions.

Route Classification 2.0 enhances earlier models by distinguishing nuanced routes like fades and screens through refined trajectory analysis. Completion Probability utilizes an XGBoost regressor trained on multiple in-play variables such as air distance and defender separation. These primitives form a unified framework where player tracking data is transformed into actionable game-theoretic signals. Each metric operates under distinct assumptions: transformers assume sequential dependencies, route classification depends on motion clarity, and completion probability assumes feature relevance. Dualities emerge in how spatial-temporal data informs both strategic intent and outcome likelihood. Failure modes include misclassification due to overlapping motion patterns, ambiguous route definitions, and out-of-domain feature combinations.
